label: H.R. 9604

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 20 - 15.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9604, titled the 'Less Bureaucracy, Better Tribal Education Act,' transfers specific federal functions, programs, grants, personnel, assets, and funds relating to Tribal education and job training from the Department of Education to the Department of the Interior. It also repeals certain provisions of the Higher Education Act of 1965 and requires the Office of Management and Budget to ensure there is no net increase in full-time equivalent federal employees as a result of the transfer.

affected_groups.effect: The Department of Education loses responsibility for specified Tribal education and job training functions, the Department of the Interior takes over those functions and receives the associated personnel and assets, and the Office of Management and Budget oversees employee counts and incidental transfers.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of Education, Department of the Interior, and Office of Management and Budget)

affected_groups.effect: Programs such as demonstration grants, professional development, language programs, career and technical education, and specific grants to institutions will be managed by the Department of the Interior instead of the Department of Education, and tribes will be consulted regarding the provisions.
affected_groups.group: Indian Tribes and Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian educational programs

key_provisions: Transfers various American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian education and job training programs from the Department of Education to the Department of the Interior.
Repeals Part J and Part Z of title VIII of the Higher Education Act of 1965.
Transfers personnel, assets, liabilities, contracts, property, and unexpended funds associated with the moved functions to the Secretary of the Interior.
Directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to ensure the Act does not cause a net increase in federal full-time equivalent employees.

Requires the Secretary of Education to consult and coordinate with Indian Tribes on the provisions of the Act within 6 months of enactment, and to publish written responses to correspondence on the Department's public website.
Sets the general effective date for the Act and its transfers to take effect one year after the Secretary of Education publishes the required written response following tribal consultations.
